Goal
* One of the contribution guidelines is "Don't address the reader directly." Accordingly, please remove or rewrite all the sentences containing "you" or "your". This is particularly important given that not everyone loves pizza or has followed the same education system.

* Please state the basis for determining cost efficiency (price per cm²) in this section. Mentioning it only in the Output section is too late and doesn't clearly connect it to the task.

* Regarding the two formulas:
  - Please define each variable.
  - Please state the value of π to use. (However, I noticed that the task can be solved without using π.)

Input
* In "Next N lines", please format "N" as a [[variable]].

* Please format the pizza sizes as {{constants}}.

* Please remove the example. An example input is automatically provided in the Example section.

Output
* Please format "[[N]] lines" in <<bold>>.

* Please replace "square centimeter" with "cm²" for consistency, as "cm" is used elsewhere in the statement.

* Please specify the required ordering of output lines when there is more than one pizza.

* Please remove the example. An example output is automatically provided in the Example section.

Constraints
* Please replace "price" with "[[price1]], [[price2]], [[price3]]".
* Please add the following constraints after the first constraint:
1 ≤ length of [[name]] ≤ 99
[[name]] contains no space characters.
Each [[name]] appears once in each case.

Stub generator
* Please add a write statement, e.g. write answer.

Cases
* These cases are the same:
  • Fancy Restaurant (Test 3)
  • Fancy Restaurant Validator (Validator 3)

* All cases pass even when the area is incorrectly calculated as A = π ⋅ d² or even A = π ⋅ (2d)². Please modify the final three pairs of cases (both tests and validators) so that these incorrect calculations produce a wrong answer for at least some pizzas.

Thanks.

Hey 5DN1L,

thanks a ton for the time you taken to give me such a detailed feedback. I really appreciate it, especially since this is my first contribution.

I already implemented every point and tried to implement the last one, when I noticed that this can't be done. Explaination:

We are comparing the relative cost per area. So P1/A1 vs. P2/A2 vs. P3/A3. 
If we multiply each denominator with a constant value, then the relative order will be the same: P1/(A1*2) vs P2/(A2*2) vs P3/(A3*2). 
A = π ⋅ d² is just A*2 and A = π ⋅ (2d)² is A*4.

That's a little disappointing, but I think it's still suitable for a clash.
Btw: Using A = π ⋅ r as a wrong formula fails (which is correct).

Again: Thank you very much!

Ah, you're absolutely correct! So ultimately, the task doesn't require using π, and could use the diameter directly without calculating the radius. That fact may be useful when playing in Shortest mode 😆

Just a few formatting changes:

Goal
* Single-line monospace formatting could make a line too long, causing it to be cut off when the browser window isn't wide enough. If you'd like to keep the monospace formatting in the final paragraph, please use multi-line formatting instead by enclosing the text in three backticks rather than single backticks, and splitting the text across multiple lines.

* Please also format all instances of "A", "r" and "d" as [[variables]], and "π" and "3.1416" as {{constants}}.

One other note: although I'm not requesting any further changes to the existing cases, please try to use a wider variety of input values when creating case pairs for clashes or puzzles in the future, rather than simply reordering the input lines.

Thanks.
